title: Impact of China's WTO Accession on Manufacturing Employment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with region and year fixed effects, leveraging China’s WTO accession in 2001 as a common policy shock. Regions more highly exposed to trade (treated=1) are compared to less exposed regions (treated=0) before vs after 2001 (post=1).
- Why: The policy timing is common, while treatment intensity (high exposure) varies across regions. DID isolates the differential change in log manufacturing employment for high-exposure regions relative to low-exposure regions around the accession.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of WTO accession, manufacturing employment in high- and low-exposure regions would have followed parallel trends.
  - No anticipatory effects: No differential pre-trends driven by anticipatory behavior prior to 2001.
  - Stable composition/SUTVA: No spillovers that differentially affect control units due to treated units’ exposure.
  - Exposure status is predetermined (based on pre-period trade integration), not endogenously changing due to the policy.

To probe the assumptions, I will:
- Include unit and time fixed effects.
- Provide an event-study style check for pre-trends.
- Add unit-specific linear trends.
- Run a pre-period placebo DID.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Load or install packages
req_pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest")
for(p in req_pkgs){
  if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)){
    install.packages(p)
  }
}
library(data.table)
library(fixest)

# 1) Read data
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s34_data.csv")

# 2) Clean and prepare
# Ensure correct types
df[, unit_id := as.integer(unit_id)]
df[, period  := as.integer(period)]
df[, treated := as.integer(treated)]
df[, post    := as.integer(post)]
df[, y       := as.numeric(y)]

# Sanity checks
if(!all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","y") %in% names(df))){
  stop("Required columns are missing.")
}

# Derive interaction to avoid relying on pre-computed column
df[, treat_post := treated * post]

# Identify policy year and reference period for event study
if(any(df$post == 1)){
  policy_year <- min(df[post == 1, period])
} else {
  stop("No post-policy observations found (post == 1).")
}
if(any(df$post == 0)){
  ref_period <- max(df[post == 0, period])
} else {
  stop("No pre-policy observations found (post == 0).")
}

# 3) Main DID: TWFE with clustering at unit level
m_main <- feols(
  y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period,
  cluster = ~ unit_id,
  data = df
)

ct_main <- coeftable(m_main)
att_hat <- unname(ct_main["treated:post", "Estimate"])
se_hat  <- unname(ct_main["treated:post", "Std. Error"])
t_hat   <- unname(ct_main["treated:post", "t value"])
p_hat   <- unname(ct_main["treated:post", "Pr(>|t|)"])

cat("Main DID (TWFE) result:\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT (treated x post) = %.4f\n  SE = %.4f, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n\n",
            att_hat, se_hat, t_hat, p_hat))

# 4) Robustness A: Event-study style differentials (pre-trend check)
# Model: y_it = alpha_i + gamma_t + sum_{tau != ref} beta_tau * 1[period=tau]*treated + eps_it
m_es <- feols(
  y ~ i(period, treated, ref = ref_period) | unit_id + period,
  cluster = ~ unit_id,
  data = df
)

cat("Event-study (differential by period for treated vs control):\n")
# Print a compact summary for a few nearest leads/lags (if present)
es_tab <- as.data.frame(coeftable(m_es))
es_tab$coef_name <- rownames(es_tab)

# Extract period numbers from coefficient names and order
# fixest naming: "period::XXXX#treated"
get_period_from_name <- function(x){
  as.integer(gsub(".*::(.*)#treated", "\\1", x))
}
es_tab$period_val <- NA_integer_
treated_rows <- grepl("#treated$", es_tab$coef_name)
es_tab$period_val[treated_rows] <- sapply(es_tab$coef_name[treated_rows], get_period_from_name)

# Identify pre and post coefficients relative to policy year (excluding ref)
es_pre  <- es_tab[treated_rows & es_tab$period_val < policy_year & es_tab$period_val != ref_period, ]
es_post <- es_tab[treated_rows & es_tab$period_val >= policy_year, ]

# Report the closest lead and first few lags if available
if(nrow(es_pre) > 0){
  es_pre <- es_pre[order(es_pre$period_val, decreasing = TRUE), ]
  head_pre <- head(es_pre, 3)
  cat("  Selected pre-period differentials (should be ~0 if parallel trends holds):\n")
  for(i in seq_len(nrow(head_pre))){
    cat(sprintf("    period=%d: coef=%.4f (SE=%.4f, p=%.4f)\n",
                head_pre$period_val[i], head_pre$Estimate[i], head_pre$`Std. Error`[i], head_pre$`Pr(>|t|)`[i]))
  }
} else {
  cat("  No additional pre-period differentials beyond the reference period to test.\n")
}

if(nrow(es_post) > 0){
  es_post <- es_post[order(es_post$period_val), ]
  head_post <- head(es_post, 3)
  cat("  Selected post-period differentials:\n")
  for(i in seq_len(nrow(head_post))){
    cat(sprintf("    period=%d: coef=%.4f (SE=%.4f, p=%.4f)\n",
                head_post$period_val[i], head_post$Estimate[i], head_post$`Std. Error`[i], head_post$`Pr(>|t|)`[i]))
  }
}
cat("\n")

# Joint test that all available pre-period differentials (leads) are zero
if(nrow(es_pre) > 0){
  # Build restriction string for fixest::wald
  Rstr <- paste(paste0("`", es_pre$coef_name, "` = 0"), collapse = " & ")
  w_pre <- tryCatch(wald(m_es, Rstr), error = function(e) NULL)
  if(!is.null(w_pre)){
    cat(sprintf("Pre-trend joint test (all pre coefficients = 0): F=%.2f, p=%.4f\n\n",
                w_pre$stat, w_pre$p.value))
  } else {
    cat("Pre-trend joint test could not be computed.\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Pre-trend joint test skipped (no pre coefficients available).\n\n")
}

# 5) Robustness B: Unit-specific linear trends
m_trend <- feols(
  y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period + unit_id[period],
  cluster = ~ unit_id,
  data = df
)

ct_trend <- coeftable(m_trend)
att_trend <- unname(ct_trend["treated:post", "Estimate"])
se_trend  <- unname(ct_trend["treated:post", "Std. Error"])
t_trend   <- unname(ct_trend["treated:post", "t value"])
p_trend   <- unname(ct_trend["treated:post", "Pr(>|t|)"])

cat("DID with unit-specific linear trends:\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT (treated x post) = %.4f\n  SE = %.4f, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n\n",
            att_trend, se_trend, t_trend, p_trend))

# 6) Robustness C: Pre-period placebo DID (split pre-period into early vs late)
df_pre <- df[period < policy_year]
pre_periods <- sort(unique(df_pre$period))
if(length(pre_periods) >= 2){
  # Choose a placebo cutoff in the middle of the pre-periods
  placebo_cutoff <- pre_periods[ceiling(length(pre_periods)/2)]
  df_pre[, placebo_post := as.integer(period >= placebo_cutoff)]
  
  m_placebo <- feols(
    y ~ treated:placebo_post | unit_id + period,
    cluster = ~ unit_id,
    data = df_pre
  )
  ct_placebo <- coeftable(m_placebo)
  att_placebo <- unname(ct_placebo["treated:placebo_post", "Estimate"])
  se_placebo  <- unname(ct_placebo["treated:placebo_post", "Std. Error"])
  t_placebo   <- unname(ct_placebo["treated:placebo_post", "t value"])
  p_placebo   <- unname(ct_placebo["treated:placebo_post", "Pr(>|t|)"])
  
  cat("Placebo DID within pre-period only:\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Placebo ATT (treated x placebo_post) = %.4f\n  SE = %.4f, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n\n",
              att_placebo, se_placebo, t_placebo, p_placebo))
} else {
  cat("Placebo DID skipped (insufficient distinct pre-periods).\n")
}

# Final clear numerical result (main estimate)
cat("Final reported effect (Main DID ATT on log employment):\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT = %.4f (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n", att_hat, se_hat, p_hat))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. WTO accession catalyzed export growth, FDI, and integration into global value chains, disproportionately benefiting more trade-exposed (often coastal) regions. These regions likely experienced higher manufacturing employment relative to less exposed regions.
- Magnitude: Moderate. I expect an ATT in the range of +0.05 to +0.12 log points (about 5–12%) in the years immediately following accession, attenuating when allowing for unit-specific trends but remaining positive and statistically meaningful if parallel trends holds.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log manufacturing employment before and after 2001 between high and low trade exposure regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Regions with higher exposure to trade experienced a positive effect on manufacturing employment following China's WTO accession.
